science.qualification: Photosphere color from a blackbody at the star's published temperature, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,151 K and log g 4.49 (u1 0.614, u2 0.153): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Jun 2013
science.description: Radial component of the star's large-scale magnetic field, fitted with ZDIpy to 19 ESPaDOnS spectra of 15 June 2013 to 1 July 2013 (reduced chi-square 1.20, against 4.1 with no field); mean field 74 G. A reduction made in this project, not a published map. Black line: 65 degrees south, below which the star never faces us.
science.title: ESPaDOnS · magnetic map made here · Jun 2013

science.label: Sector 81
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 4.65 days, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 81 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 7.2%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.54%, the light's own noise being 0.08%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. In this sector the method of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) finds a period of 4.81 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.31, a width of 0.45 and a fit of 1.00, and in all 2 of the star's sectors together a period of 4.65 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.26, a width of 0.48 and a fit of 0.99; its criteria accept that as the star's rotation. The map is made at the tilt the page draws the star with, 65°. Gaia DR3 lists 37 other stars within 63 arcseconds, with 3.1% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 81

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffe8d5, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 81 (July and August 2024): the map's scale, 85% to 115% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 22.6% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · July and August 2024
